findings.title: Node-scoped verification loads the v1 graph instead of the v2 write sets
findings.criterion_ref: PKG-T05 — “--node must not … skip a file within its node's write set that either whole-tree scope would have scanned.”
findings.trigger: The graph executes any declared N20–N50 scanner command. Those commands pass `--node` but omit `--graph implementation.graph.v2.yaml`, so the scanner loads its default v1 graph.
findings.consequence: N20's verification skips the newly N20-owned `runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py` and `tests/runtime/test_plan26_egress.py`. N20 can therefore pass its node-scoped scan while either owned file contains a prohibited reference; N30 conversely scans those paths using its obsolete v1 ownership.
findings.evidence: `implementation.graph.v2.yaml` lines 166, 186, 209, and 231 omit `--graph`. `controller/check_forbidden_production_refs.py` lines 434–446 defaults `--graph` to `DEFAULT_GRAPH_PATH`; `controller/core.py` line 28 defines that as `implementation.graph.v1.yaml`. `controller/scheduler.py` lines 486–488 executes verification argv unchanged. A direct invocation reported graph digest `ec414f…`, the v1 digest, and omitted both egress paths from N20's scanned files, whereas validation artifact `results/v2/validation/04_node_scan_N20_full.json` includes them only because that validation used the v2 graph explicitly.

observations: The v2 header also changes `source_incident` from the v1 postmortem path to the specification-correction result, although the falsification note says only `version`, `source_spec`, and `result_pattern` should change at header level. No numbered criterion constrains `source_incident`, so this does not block independently.

`tools/validate_plan.py --graph implementation.graph.v2.yaml` reports `valid: true` because its scanner-command check accepts `--node <ID>` without requiring the command to bind the graph being validated. Tightening that structural check would catch PKG-QA-001, but this is hardening rather than a separate finding.
reasoning: Direct graph and prompt inspection confirmed the requested ownership transfer, unique write sets, v2 result roots, source-spec binding, and N60's unchanged bare scan. Historical hashes/evidence were consistent with the pre-recovery state, and git status showed no implementation-path changes. The surviving defect is operational: the node scanner itself narrows correctly when given v2, but the package's actual verification commands silently give it v1, defeating PKG-T05.
